FADRILAN DIL.G-Region No. 822 Quezon Avenue, Barangay 94 Paligsahan, Quezon City Dear Dir. Fadrilan: This has reference to your Memorandum dated 24 August 2016 informing the SILG that based on the facts presented and upon evaluation of the matter, you concur with the recommendation of DI I.G-Occidental Mindoro Provincial Office in recommending the recognition of the appointment of Dr. Myrna Zapanta as member of the Sangguniang Bayan of San Jose, Occidental Mindoro. Based on the documents forwarded to the Central Office and subsequent verifications thereon with your good Office, hereunder are the relevant factual antecedents: l) Philip Lim ran for the position of Sangguniang Bayan Member, San Jose, Occidental Mindoro, in the last 09 May Synchronized National and Local Elections under the banner of Liberal Party; 2) Lim won as the 8th-ranking Sangguniang Bayan Member but died prior to his assumption to office; 3) In a letter dated 28 June 2016, Atty. Manuelito R. I .una informed Governor Mario Gene Mendiola, Occidental Mindoro that the latter should desist from making any appointment considering that Lim has yet to become a member of the Sangguniang Bayan for a new term so that Section 45 (a) (2) of the Local Government Code of 1991 finds no application; His client, outgoing Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Marian Haydee G. Villaroza, who plaéecl 9th in the Sangguniang Bayan race last 09 May 2016 Synchronized National and Local Elections, will vie for the position left by deceased Lim; 4) On 19 July 2016, Dr. Myrna Zapanta, upon nomination by the Liberal Party, was appointed by the Provincial Governor as member of the Sangguniang Bayan of San

Jose, Occidental Mindoro. Said appointment was anchored upon Section 45, Paragraph (a), Subsection 2 of the Local Government Code of 1991. In sum, the issues to be resolved herein are as follows: l. Since Lim died prior to his assumption as member of the Sangguniang Bayan of San Jose, is Section 45 (a)(2) of the Local Government Code of 1991, pertaining to the appointment by the Governor of permanent: vacancies in the sangguniang bayan where automatic successions do not apply, apply? and 2. Is outgoing Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Marian Haydee G. Villaroza, who placed 9th in the Sangguniang Bayan race last 09 May 2016 Synchronized National and Local Elections, qualified to be appointed to the position left by deceased Lim? We shall answer the foregoing issues in one (I) discussion. Per our verification with DILG-Occidental Mindoro, Lim was already proclaimed winner by the Municipal Board of Canvassers before he died. Such proclamation would only mean that he acquired a plurality of the votes lawfully cast sufficient to elect him to said position. "The fact of having a plurality of votes lawfully cast is what confers the title to the office, xxx. "(Mechem, note 2 at 130, cited in De Leon, H. Jr. Law on Public Offices and Election Law, 1990 Edition, p. 374). Subsequent to one's election to office and before entering upon the performance of his duties, the person so elected is usually required by law to do some acts by which he shall signify his acceptance of the office and his undertaking to execute the trust confided in him. Section 92 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) provides and we quote: SECTION 92. out/l.— (a) AI/ elective and appointive local officials and employees shall, upon assumption to office, subscribe to an oath or affirmation of office in the prescribed form. xxx Such act wherein the person elected shall signify his acceptance of the office and his undertaking to execute the trust confided in him is ordinarily termed qualification. It generally consists of the taking, and often of subscribing and filing of an ollicial oath. Accordingly, fililure to take an oath and assume the powers, duties and functions of the office would result to a failure to qualify, which, in turn, is one of the grounds enumerated uncler Section 44 of the Local Government Code that would render an office permanently vacant. Said provision provides and we quote: Section 44. Permanent Vacancies in the Offices of the Go vernor, Vice-Governor, Mayor, and Vice-Mayor. xxv For purposes of this Chapter, a permanent vacancy arises when an elective local official fills a higher vacant office, refbses to assume office,

to quality, dies, is removed from office, voluntarily resigns, or is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the fimctions of his office. For purposes of succession as provided in [his Chapter, ranking in the sanggunian shall he determined on the basis OT the proportion OT votes obtained by each winning candidate to the total number of registered voters in each district in the immediately preceding local election. (Emphasis Supplied) DILG-Occidental Mindoro was correct in applying the aforequoted provision of Section 44 to the herein case 01' deceased Lim. Lim was not able to assume and take his oath of office come noon of 30 June 2016. His failure to assume and take his oath will result to his failure to qualify as 8th-ranking Sangguniang Bayan Member. Since there is failure to qualify on his part, this would thereafter render his position permanently vacant and there being a permanent vacancy in the 8th-ranking or the last-ranking Sangguniang Bayan Member, the rule on the filling-up by appointment where automatic successions do not apply under Section 45 of' the Local Government Code of 1991, is therefore applicable, thus: SECTION 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian.—(a) Permanent vacancies the sanggunian where automatic successionsprovided above in [he following manner: XXX (2) Ubegoverpor, in the case of the component cicies and the sangguniang bayan; XXX (b) Except nor the sangguniang barangay, on lv the nominee of the povitica/ party under which the sanggunian member concerned had been elected and whose elevation to the position next higher in rank created the last vacancy in the sanggunian shall be appointed in the manner hereinabove provided. The appointee shall come the same political party as that of the sanggunian member who caused the vacancy and shall serve the unexpired term of [he vacant office. In the appointment herein mentioned, a nomination and a cenificate of' membership of the appointee from the highest official of the political party concerned are conditions sine qua non, and any appointment without such nomination and certification shall' be null and void ab initio and shall be a ground Tor administrative action against the official responsible therefor. xxx xvx xxx (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the foregoing, the party under which the Lim had been elected shall be the basis of the appointment of' his replacement. It may be well to stress, at this juncture, that per the documents submitted to the Central Office, Dr. Myrna Zapanta was duly nominated by the Liberal Party, the same party under which deceased Lim had been elected and duly appointed by the Provincial

Governor of Occidental Mindoro. Since the process for the filling-up of vacancy as se forth under the albrequoted Section 45 of [he Code was already completed, said appointment of Dr. Zapanta enjoys the presumption of regularity, unless declared otherwise by a competent court upon filing of a proper remedy. Nowhere can we find in pertinent laws that the permanent vacancy shall be filled- up by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) in a special election as suggested by Atty. Luna in his 28 June 2016 letter to Governor Mendiola. The only cases that we can recall where a special election is needed are those provided under the Omnibus Election Code (BP 881), such as the following: (l) Section Postponement of Election; (2) Section 6- Failure of Election; and (3) Section 7- Call of Special Election in case of Vacancy in the offices of' the President and Vice-President, Senate and House of Representatives. 'l'o our mind, the reason why there is no provision providing for a special election on vacancies in the local elective positions is that such cases are already addressed by the rules under the aforequoted Sections 44 and 45 of the Local Government Code of 1991. Nowhere can we also find in pertinent laws or even in jurisprudence that in case of permanent vacancy in the sangguniang bayan under the same circumstance, the next-in- rank in the election shall be appointed as such. In fact, in many jurisprudence decided by the Supreme Court, said Court maintained on the contrary, that is, the non-proclamation of the defeated candidate or second placer simply means he lost in the election. Further, since Marian Haydee G. Villaroza lost in his bid as Sangguniang Bayan Member in the last 09 May 2016 Elections, it may also be worthy to consider the following provisions of law and issuance: Section 94, Local Government Code of' 1991 "SECTION 94. Appointment OT Elective and Appointive Local Officials; Candidate Who Lost in an Election. —xxx (b) Except for losing candidates in barangay elections, no candidate who lost in any election shall, within one (1) year afier such election, be appointed to anv office in the Governmem or any government- owned or-controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries. Section 4, Rule XIII, Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Actions (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998, as amended) "Section 4. person WII o los t in an election (except Ba rangay election) shall not be eligible for appointment or reemployment to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporation within one year following such election.
